source.title: Making Analog Training Scale: Co-Designing Mapping, Optimizer, and Converters
source.authors: Zhao-Xian Wu; Tayfun Gokmen; Omobayode I. Fagbohungbe; T. Xiao; Tian-Yi Chen

record.tranche_reason: The study uses a different training system and evaluates whether language-model validation loss follows scaling fits across model sizes, tokens, and compute.
record.gate_note: The study reports scaling-fit exponents and downstream screening accuracies. Individual scaling endpoints are plotted but not reported as exact values, so they are not entered as separate numeric rows. The downstream tables' per-task scores are omitted; the study's aggregate Avg scores are recorded. The Chinchilla token allocation is used as a schedule, not optimized as an allocation experiment.
record.test_reason: The study fits held-out OpenWebText validation loss as L = AX^-α across five model scales (6.8M–123.6M), for a matched digital AdamW baseline and for simulated analog in-memory training. This is a new training substrate with a direct result on V1. It also reports zero-shot downstream accuracy across the same scales, which bears weakly on V6.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The main text, however, states more strongly that the architecture 'sustains predictable scaling dynamics across orders of magnitude'. The appendix calls the fits preliminary guides that cannot isolate exponents or establish an asymptotic law. The authors describe the downstream screens as descriptive and task- and scale-dependent, and note that digital pretraining loss stays lower.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates hardware-calibrated analog in-memory training with digital weight-gradient accumulation, logical-space AdamW, analog MVMs, and converter management; the matched reference uses digital AdamW. The scaling fits use five completed schedules and ordinary least squares in log loss–log coordinate space.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported scaling fits use five completed endpoints and ordinary least squares in log L–log X space; the authors state that model size, processed data, and compute covary and that the fit omits an irreducible-loss term.

fits_no_version.finding: Analog in-memory training with hardware non-idealities reproduces nearly the same loss-scaling exponents as digital training, with a constant-offset loss gap.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Scaling-law exponents are preserved under noisy, low-precision training hardware; non-idealities shift the prefactor, not the exponent.

record.problems: The main scaling experiments use one random seed per condition, leaving run-to-run variability and scaling-fit uncertainty unquantified. Fits use only five completed endpoints, omit an irreducible-loss term, and use covarying size, token, and compute schedules. The reported results are architecture-level simulations, not physical-hardware training.
record.rows_left_out: Individual model-scale validation-loss points and plotted trajectories in Figure 6 are not recorded separately because exact endpoint values are not stated in the text or tables. Per-task zero-shot scores in Tables 4–5 are omitted; aggregate Avg scores are recorded instead.

untested.parts: Several orders of magnitude (only ~1.3 decades in N, ~2.6 in compute). Separate N or D laws with the other held non-bottleneck (coordinates covary). No fit-quality or seed variance reported.
Fits are dashed out to 10x the largest coordinate, but no larger run validates them.
Uses a fixed ~20N token rule; no allocation search.
Depth sweeps on Shakespeare change parameter count; no fixed-N shape comparison.
No other modality, repeated-data, fine-tuning or transfer regime; analog hardware is a substrate change within text pretraining.
No relation between downstream accuracy and pretraining loss; sub-130M models on near-chance tasks only.
Fitting method, parameter counting and schedule are not varied.

missing.what: Numeric validation losses at Tiny/Small/Medium for Digital Adam (6.3451, 5.3033, 4.5499) and the full recipe +init (6.6075, 5.6245, 4.8696). These give local N-exponents of ~0.21–0.25 consistent with the fits, and the only numeric endpoints reported.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V5 links and labels are dropped. Hardware substrate is not a new modality or data regime, so the analog result is placed under V1 and fits_no_version. The tranche is changed from T2 to T3 because the result is in a new setting. Individual V6 rows are judged against the Tiny checkpoint of the same path and suite. Differences of 1–3 points on 128-example subsets of near-chance tasks are likely within noise. All runs are single-seed. Reported losses (~4.5–6.6) are high for OpenWebText, consistent with very short 20N schedules.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not independently vary parameters, tokens, and compute; the schedules covary. It does not establish behavior over several orders of magnitude or an asymptotic law.
The fits are extended to ten times the largest observed coordinate as preliminary guides, but no larger run is reported to validate those predictions.
The study follows an approximately 20N token schedule; it does not search for or compare loss-minimizing parameter/token allocations at fixed compute.
No controlled comparison varies depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.

The tested setting is decoder-only language-model training from scratch on OpenWebText using simulated analog hardware. Other modalities, fine-tuning, transfer, and repeated-data regimes are not tested.
The study reports zero-shot screening accuracy on two task suites, not a comprehensive downstream-task evaluation or a direct relationship between task performance and pretraining loss.
The study does not vary fitting methods, parameter-counting choices, or training setups to test whether exponents or compute-optimal allocations depend on those choices.

relationships.condition: Digital AdamW nanoGPT on OpenWebText, 6.8M–123.6M params, ~20N tokens, single seed
relationships.reason: Power-law fits give α=0.238 (N), 0.237 (tokens) and 0.117 (compute) over the narrow tested range (r2, r4, r6).
relationships.display_finding: Digital training gives power-law exponents 0.238 for parameters, 0.237 for tokens and 0.117 for compute over the narrow tested range.

relationships.condition: Simulated analog in-memory training (Li-ECRAM tiles, S-OUT recipe), same models and schedules
relationships.reason: Analog loss also follows power-law fits with near-identical exponents (0.231, 0.230, 0.114), though loss stays higher at every scale (r1, r3, r5).
relationships.display_finding: Analog training gives corresponding exponents 0.231, 0.230 and 0.114, while loss remains higher at every scale.

relationships.condition: Digital checkpoints, two zero-shot screening suites (128-example subsets, many tasks near chance)
relationships.reason: Averages rise only 2–4 pts over 18x params and plateau or dip after Medium, not a clean scale trend (r8–r11, r18–r21).
relationships.display_finding: Average scores rose only 2–4 points over an 18-fold parameter increase and plateaued or declined after Medium.

relationships.reason: Table 4 average is flat to non-monotonic (37.0→34.8→37.6). Table 5 gains only at XLarge (+3.0) with a dip at Large (r12–r16, r22–r26).
relationships.display_finding: One suite progressed through 37.0, 34.8 and 37.6, while the other gained only at XLarge by 3.0 points after a decline at Large.
